messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Keeping unused variables in addition to grouping variable in ddply dataframe output
parts:
Hello all,

I have what seems like a super simple problem but I can't seem to
figure out the right search terms. I need to summarize some data but I
would like to keep the variables that I am not using to as groups in
the resulting data frames. For example say I have the following
dataframe:


dat1 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 125), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="here")
dat2 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 200), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="there")
dat <- rbind(dat1,dat2)
str(dat)

## I want the max value of x for each group ("site") for all year
## No problem, I can do this using ddply like so

library(plyr)
ddply(dat, c("site"), function(df) return(c(max=max(df$x))))

## Now problem is that I also want to know what year and what jday
corresponds to this max value.
## So my question is: How do I keep these variables in my resulting dataframe?

Thanks so much in advance!

Sam

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Keeping unused variables in addition to grouping variable in ddply dataframe output

The easiest way is to use subset:

ddply(dat, c("site"), subset, x == max(df))

Hadley

On Tue, Jan 10, 2012 at 9:24 AM, Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu> wrote:
> Hi Sam,
>
> The easiest way is to use subset:
>
> ddply(dat, c("site"), subset, x == max(df))

I don't think that can work as df is not defined, you probably need

ddply(dat, c("site"), function(df) subset(df, x == max(x)))

I was hoping to find a way with summarize,

ddply(dat, c("site"), summarize, max = max(x))

but it doesn't seem possible to refer to previous transformations when
creating new variables (as mutate does),

ddply(dat, c("site"), summarize, max = max(x), year = year[x==max])
# fails

Would it be possible in theory to combine this feature of mutate with summarize?

Cheers,

baptiste

You're trying to select the values of x that are equal to mean(x) or
sd(x), but there may be none that satisfy this condition. In contrast,
there is always an element that is the minimum or maximum.

messages.author: f719e20ffd7dbb8d
messages.subject: Re: Keeping unused variables in addition to grouping variable in ddply dataframe output
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to do something similar, but I'm summarizing given a certain variable (make) and would like to retain the year.

I can get the summary, with no year retained this way:

mean_MPG_allyears = ddply(mean_MPG, c("make"), summerise, mean.count = mean(mean.count))

The variables in mean_MPG are VClass, make, year, mean.count.

On Monday, January 9, 2012 3:21:57 PM UTC-5, Sam wrote:
Hello all,

I have what seems like a super simple problem but I can't seem to
figure out the right search terms. I need to summarize some data but I
would like to keep the variables that I am not using to as groups in
the resulting data frames. For example say I have the following
dataframe:


dat1 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 125), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="here")
dat2 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 200), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="there")
dat <- rbind(dat1,dat2)
str(dat)

## I want the max value of x for each group ("site") for all year
## No problem, I can do this using ddply like so

library(plyr)
ddply(dat, c("site"), function(df) return(c(max=max(df$x))))

## Now problem is that I also want to know what year and what jday
corresponds to this max value.
## So my question is: How do I keep these variables in my resulting dataframe?

Thanks so much in advance!

Sam

On Sun, Nov 17, 2013 at 3:26 PM, Jessica Clark <jessie...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I'm trying to do something similar, but I'm summarizing given a certain
> variable (make) and would like to retain the year.
>
> I can get the summary, with no year retained this way:
>
> mean_MPG_allyears = ddply(mean_MPG, c("make"), summerise, mean.count =
> mean(mean.count))
>
> The variables in mean_MPG are VClass, make, year, mean.count.

It is unclear to me whether you want

ddply(mean_MPG, c("make"), function(df) return(with(df,
data.frame(year = year mean.count=mean(mean.count)))))

or

ddply(mean_MPG, c("make", "year"), summarize, mean.count = mean(mean.count))

but probably one of those it what you are looking for.

Best,
Ista
